reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification (steps grouped by the numbered source lines that carry the mathematical content; lines 0001-0257 and the tikz block 1041-1101 are LaTeX preamble/figure code with no mathematical claim).
L0259-0261 (strongly connected components): defining X_0=cube_1 and adjoining cubes meeting X_n in >1 vertex is well posed; if the waffle were a union of several such components they meet in single vertices, local finiteness makes such a vertex P a local cut point, and simple connectivity upgrades this to a global cut point (no cycle can reconnect the pieces), contradicting quasi-isometry to H^2. Justified (the last implication is terse but standard for a one-ended CAT(0) cube complex).
L0263-0274 (extension of the combinatorialization): two maximal cubes sharing an m-face have combinatorial maps agreeing on 0-skeleta, hence agreeing on the common face; induction over X_n covers the whole (strongly connected) waffle; the resulting map is a local isometry, hence a covering map of complete simply connected spaces, hence an isometry. Justified ('sqphi_n: X_n -> X_n' is a typo for X_n -> waffle_2).
L0277-0279 (Definition of combinatorialization): a definition; well posed given the preceding step.
L0290-0299 (section setup): recollection of the tree-of-spaces picture and the statement that hyperplanes are CAT(0) cube complexes (Sageev); no new claim proved here.
L0304-0311 (Prop. strands, statement): statement only; verified against its proof below, except the 'furthermore' clause (sigma is an axis for EVERY hyperbolic isometry of X), which the proof does not actually establish -- an unproved side remark, not used in the steps that follow.
L0318-0324 (2-ended types): correct dichotomy for 2-ended groups (virtually Z surjects to Z or to D_infty); Gamma^+ well defined.
L0330-0334 (CAT(0) circumcentre): correct quotation of Bridson-Haefliger II.2.7.
L0347-0361 (BH II.6.8): correct quotation (parallel axes = Min(g); Min(g)=Y x R with g acting as (y,t)->(y,t+|g|); commuting isometries preserve Min(g) and split).
L0367-0377: K=ker(pi) is finite since Gamma is 2-ended; conjugation by g gives an automorphism of the finite group K, so g^n centralizes K when n is the exponent of Aut(K); g^n then is central in Gamma^+=<g,K>, so by BH II.6.8(3) Gamma^+ preserves Min(g^n)=Y x R. Justified.
L0379-0387: each element of Gamma^+ projects to an isometry of the CAT(0) space Y; Y is bounded because Y x R is convex in the 2-ended X; the circumcentre of the bounded set Y is fixed by the (Y-)image Gamma', so the fixed set Y_0 is nonempty. Justified.
L0389-0402 (independence of the choice of g): any other lift g' satisfies (g')^n = g^n k with k in K; since g^n is central, (g')^n preserves Min(g^n); its R-component must translate by |g^n| because the K-part has finite order; on Y_0 the Y-component acts trivially, giving Y_0 x R inside Min((g')^n), and the symmetric argument gives equality. Justified (terse but correct).
L0404-0407 (Z-type case): sigma = {c_{Y_0}} x R with c_{Y_0} the circumcentre of Y_0 is canonical and Gamma-invariant. Justified.
L0408-0426 (dihedral case, claim r.rho_x is in Min(g^n)): the computation g^n r x = r (r^{-1} g^n r) x = r g^{-n} k x = r g^{-n} x is correct, using that k in K acts trivially on Y_0 x R (its Y-part is in Gamma' and its R-part has finite order); hence d(rx, g^n r x) = d(x, g^{-n} x) = |g^n|, so r x realises the translation length. Justified.
L0428-0442: independence of the choice of the reflection lift r (r'=k'r=rk, and K acts trivially on Y_0 x R); g r . rho_x = r g^{-1} k . rho_x = r . rho_x, so r.rho_x is Gamma^+-invariant and therefore of the form {q} x R with q in Y_0; hence Y_0 x R is Gamma-invariant, Gamma acts on Y_0, its fixed set Y_1 is nonempty (same circumcentre argument as before), and sigma = {c_{Y_1}} x R is canonical and Gamma-invariant. Justified.
L0447-0459 (Lemma, strand classification, statement): statement only.
L0461-0471: if K_sigma acts freely on sigma it is Z-type (infinite dihedral cannot act freely on a line); an element fixing x in sigma induces an isometry of the visual circle at x preserving {sigma^+,sigma^-}, and the subgroup of Isom(S^1) preserving a 2-point set is at most Z_2 + Z_2; faithfulness on the boundary then gives |(K_sigma)_x| in {1,2,4}. Justified.
L0473-0485 (case analysis): discrete cocompact action on a line has quotient a circle or a segment; circle case forces point stabilisers to fix sigma pointwise, giving Z + Z_2 (the pointwise-fixing Z_2 is canonical, hence central, and the extension by Z splits); segment case with |K_x|=4 gives (Z semidirect Z_2) + Z_2, with |K_x|=2 gives Z semidirect Z_2. Justified (the case |K_0| trivial in the circle case is just the free case already handled).
L0488-0514 (strand types): a definition; consistent with the lemma.
L0521-0529 (churro-waffle space): a definition; well posed since the strands of the preceding proposition are canonical, hence equivariant.
L0544-0557 (horostrip): a definition; the 'long side' is the boundary at the smaller height y_1, which is indeed the longer one since ds = |dx|/y.
L0571-0598 (quadrilaterals): with alpha(t)=(t,y_1), beta(t)=(t,y_2), the hyperbolic lengths are (b-a)/y_1 and (b-a)/y_2, so |ln(len(alpha)/len(beta))| = |ln(y_2/y_1)| = width, and each vertical leaf has length int_{y_1}^{y_2} dt/t = ln(y_2/y_1). The vertical lines x=const are geodesics of H^2. Verified by direct computation.
L0601-0603 (equal width strips are isometric): correct (translate/scale by z -> (z-x_0)y_1'/y_1).
L0610-0622 (translation lengths): well defined since h_churro preserves each strand; tau_core is the arithmetic mean of the tau_{sigma_i}. Definition, consistent.
L0624-0644 (churro metric): width |ln(tau_core/tau_{sigma_i})| with the long side glued to whichever of core/strand has the larger translation length -- consistent with the length ratio computed in L0571-0598 (the longer side is the one at the smaller height); the Euclidean strip is used in the degenerate equal-length case; the core sides are then glued length-preservingly. Consistent.
L0646-0663 (Lemma, clutching ratios determine the metric): the r_ij determine the tau_{sigma_i} up to a common scale mu; the mean tau_core scales by the same mu; the metric depends only on the ratios tau_core/tau_{sigma_i}, which are scale-invariant. Justified.
L0667-0672 (remark that horospheres are not convex): correct and relevant caveat.
L0674-0686 (global path metric): a definition; the gluing is length-compatible along strands by the previous definition, so the path metric is well defined.
L0688-0726 (Prop., Gamma acts by isometries): the only issue is the churro stabiliser <h_churro>; on the flap F_i the arc of sigma_i from x_i to h x_i has length tau_{sigma_i}, so by the quadrilateral proposition the opposite core arc has length tau_{sigma_i} * (tau_core/tau_{sigma_i}) = tau_core, independent of i; hence the flapwise parabolic maps (x,y) -> (x+h,y) agree on the common core and assemble to an isometry. Justified.
L0731-0750 (strand/flap subdivisions, core and strand vertices): definitions; well posed.
L0752-0766 (generalized Dehn twists): a definition; well posed since the attaching maps are equivariantly re-post-composed with translations of the core.
L0768-0808 (Lemma, partial twist): the twisted attaching maps do not change the underlying topology up to quasi-isometry, and the push-forward of paths gives back a free deck action of Gamma with an equivariant path metric; cocompactness leaves only finitely many possible cellular decompositions minimizing the number of Gamma-orbits of core vertices. Justified at the level of detail given.
L0810-0845 (Assembly Lemma): given (i) tree isomorphism, (ii) waffle-wise isometry, (iii) preservation of clutching ratios, Lemma L0646-0663 makes corresponding churros isometric, equivariant strand subdivisions can be chosen per isometry class, and Lemma L0768-0808 supplies the finitely many twists making the two spaces isometric and cell-isomorphic. Justified.
L0849-0853 (Remark): items (1),(2) of the Assembly Lemma follow from the cited earlier propositions; (3) deferred to the clutching section. Consistent bookkeeping.
L0892-0901 (D-coarse intersection): a definition; the displayed identity with N_D(alpha) cap N_D(beta) is correct.
L0904-0913 (finite diameter of coarse intersections): in a hyperbolic space an infinite-diameter coarse intersection of two bi-infinite geodesics forces a common endpoint. Justified.
L0915-0942 (uniform bound N(D)): moving a witness point x into a compact coarse fundamental domain A by g in Isom(waffle) puts g.alpha, g.beta into N_{2D}(A); only finitely many strands meet that set, so the maximum of the finitely many M(alpha,beta,D) is a uniform bound. Justified.
L0944-0984 (Pattern preserving is close to isometry): x lies in a cube crossed by two hyperplanes, so x is in the D_1-coarse intersection of the two corresponding strands; the combinatorialization sends those strands to the images sigma_1', sigma_2', so sqphi(x) lies in the D_1-coarse intersection of the images; stability of quasi-geodesics puts phi(sigma_i) in a D_3-neighbourhood of sigma_i', and d(phi(x),phi(sigma_i)) <= K D_1 + C, so phi(x) lies in the D_5-coarse intersection, whose diameter is bounded by N(D_5). Justified; note two harmless typos ('phi(sigma_i')' should be 'phi(sigma_i)', 'h(sigma_i)' should be 'phi(sigma_i)') and that D_2 is defined but not used.
L0991-1023 (closest-point projections agree coarsely): the tripod comparison gives |alpha_2|=|gamma_1|=|gamma_2|=|beta_2|; quasiconvexity supplies z in Y with d(x,z) <= |alpha_1|+delta+R, and minimality of the projection gives |alpha_1|+|alpha_2| <= |alpha_1|+delta+R, i.e. |alpha_2| <= delta+R, whence d(pi_Y x, pi_Y' x) = 2|alpha_2| <= 2(delta+R). Justified.
L1025-1031 (Prop., quasi-isometries preserve clutching ratios, statement): statement only.
L1037-1039: sqphi_i sends sigma_i to sigma_{i'} by the previous proposition; the leaf-crossing involutions omega, omega' are well defined because vertical leaves foliate the flaps. Justified.
L1104-1105: replacing h_churro by a large power so that the relevant orbit points are distinct, and adjusting the pattern-matching projections by a bounded amount so that pi_i phi^{-1} phi fixes the orbits, is legitimate (all changes are bounded and finitely many conditions are imposed). Justified.
L1106-1107: existence of bounded pattern-matching projections pi_{i'} and of the bounded 'inverse' pi^{-1}_{1'} with pi^{-1}_{1'}(x') = phi(x) is a bounded modification of the identity; legitimate.
L1109: psi_1^{(n)} restricted to waffle_{1'} is a quasi-isometry quasimatching sigma_{1'} to itself, so its combinatorialization stabilises sigma_{1'} without fixed points; since g translates sigma_{1'} by a', some g^{m_n} lands within a'/2 of the image of x'. Justified (the stated domain 'waffle_1' is a typo for waffle_{1'}).
L1111: d(phi(x),phi(h^n x)) -> infinity forces d(x', g^{m_n} x') -> infinity, hence m_n -> infinity. Justified.
L1113: psi_1^{(n)}(x') = pi_{1'} phi(h^n x) by the chain of definitions, so phi(h^n x) is at uniformly bounded distance from the combinatorialized image, hence from Q_n = g^{m_n} x' (using Prop. comb-close). Justified.
L1115: d(y', omega'(Q_n)) = d(y', g^{m_n} y') = m_n b' is correct since g commutes with the leaf involution; and P_n with d(y',P_n) = m_n a' (b/a) does lie between y' and omega'(Q_n) exactly under the WLOG a/b > a'/b'. Correct, and the factor b/a is the right one: crossing a churro from sigma_1 to sigma_2 rescales lengths by (tau_core/a)(b/tau_core) = b/a.
L1117 (final contradiction): the chain phi(h^n y) ~ phi(h^n x) ~ Q_n ~ omega'(Q_n) (the last because the leaf through Q_n is a g-translate of the leaf through x') and phi(h^n y) ~ sqphi_2(omega(sqphi_1^{-1}(Q_n))) = P_n is correct, so phi(h^n y) is boundedly close to both P_n and omega'(Q_n). ERRATUM: the displayed value d(P_n, omega'(Q_n)) = m_n (a/b - a'/b') is not the actual distance, which is m_n (b' - a' b/a) = m_n a' (b'/a' - b/a) = m_n (a b' - a' b)/a; the printed expression equals m_n (a b' - a' b)/(b b'), i.e. the correct distance times the positive constant a/(b b'). Both expressions have the same sign and both tend to infinity with m_n under the standing assumption a/b > a'/b', so the contradiction with the uniform bound, and hence the conclusion a/b = a'/b', is unaffected. I record this as a typographical slip in a constant, not a failure of the argument. (Also 'omega(Q_n)' in the same line should read omega'(Q_n).)
L1152-1156 (Corollary): combines the Assembly Lemma with the cleaning proposition to pass to clean finite-index subgroups; the conclusion 'virtually act by automorphisms on a common complex' follows. Justified (the corollary mixes the letters Delta and Gamma with H and Gamma of the preceding statement -- a notational slip only).
L1169-1189 (section setup): identification of Isom(chuwaf Gamma) with the cell-complex automorphism group, the bipartite tree T, the identification of vertex/edge groups, and the remark that vertex stabilisers may be non-discrete while the automorphism groups of individual pieces are discrete, are all consistent with the construction.
L1191-1196 (groupings): a definition, following Bass-Kulkarni.
L1206-1226 (graphs of actions, covering complex, pieces): definitions; well posed (the 'S^e_v subset piece y' contains an obvious typo for piece u).
L1228-1235 (quotient graph of spaces): the quotient of the tree of spaces by G is a graph of spaces with the stated vertex and edge spaces; correct.
L1239-1257 (anatomy of a churro; discreteness): churros carry a cocompact cell structure so Aut(churro) is discrete, while G_churro need not be, because the representation G_churro -> Aut(churro) can have large kernel. Correct.
L1297-1317 (purely flapping elements, flap families, churro classes): definitions; flap families are exactly the G^0_churro-orbits of flaps, so they are permuted by G_churro. Well posed.
L1322-1327 (Lemma, core action): contrapositive is immediate -- an element acting trivially on the core is purely flapping and hence preserves every flap family. Justified ('obvious' is accurate).
L1341-1347 (low power abelian groups): definition. ERRATUM: the inner sum is printed as bigoplus_{j=1}^{e_k}, which should be e_i; as literally printed, |L(n)| = prod p_i^{e_k} differs from n whenever the exponents differ (e.g. n=12 would give C_2 + C_3 of order 6). This is a clear index typo -- every subsequent use is of a group of order n, i.e. the e_i reading -- so I do not treat it as a substantive failure.
L1349-1364 (Lemma, properties of low power abelian groups): with the intended definition, L(n) has order n and hence acts freely and transitively on any n-element set by the regular action (the appeal to Cayley's theorem is loose but the statement is right); L(n) + L(m) = L(nm) since exponents add; a subgroup of an elementary abelian p-group of rank e is elementary abelian of rank at most e, so subgroups are again low power abelian; and L(n) is determined by n via unique factorisation. Justified.
L1368-1375: Z_churro is the image of G_churro in the discrete isometry group of the core line, hence Z or infinite dihedral; a minimal set of orbit representatives of flaps exists by cocompactness. Justified.
L1376-1400: the permutation representation rho_{F_i} of Z_churro on the churro class of the flap family is well defined; the decomposition of G_churro . F_i into the disjoint union of the translated flap families is correct; choosing one flap in each translate defines an action because rho is a homomorphism; a stabilising element extends over the flap as a translation (infinite order) or reflection (order 2). Justified.
L1402-1421: choosing a free transitive L(n_i)-action on each flap family (legitimate by the lemma) and extending it to fix the core pointwise, then combining with the Z_churro-action to get a Z_churro + L(n_i) action, is consistent; the two actions commute because L(n_i) is purely flapping. Justified as far as the excerpt goes -- the source is truncated in mid-display at line 1421, so the completion of the basic grouping is not part of the text under review.
Overall: every substantive step is justified. The two genuine errata (the constant in the displayed distance at L1117 and the summation index at L1345), plus a handful of notational typos (L0268, L0973, L0971, L1109, L1117, L1153, L1214), are transcription-level slips that do not affect any conclusion: at L1117 the printed and correct expressions are positive multiples of one another and both diverge, and at L1345 every use of L(n) is as a group of order n. Verdict VALID.
